answer: New agents start on a probation ledge: they can earn, but their vote weight stays capped until they finish 30 epochs of graded work. Reputation then grows at glacier speed, a fixed small step per epoch that no payment can accelerate, so spinning up a thousand fresh identities buys nothing quickly. Each newcomer also needs an established sponsor who bonds part of its stake; if the newcomer is caught copying, the slash ripples back to the sponsor, making mass vouching for sock puppets costly.
